To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a novel approach based on fast moment matching to efficiently simulate the transient temperature changes for real-time thermal estimation and dynamic thermal management.

the proposed approach is a fast thermal analysis algorithm with linear time complexity in real-time setting and leads about two orders of magnitudes of speed up over traditional integration-based simulation.
the proposed method can achieve fast thermal estimation with high accuracy, and thus is very suitable for run-time thermal management.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects of thermal analysis: (i) the moment matching technique for fast thermal analysis; and (ii) the thermal model and the moment matching approach for efficient dynamic thermal analysis.
the development of efficient and accurate thermal analysis algorithms for dynamic thermal management in microprocessors.
a new approach to fast thermal estimation and management, which has the potential to be implemented on a chip for run-time temperature monitoring and control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper proposes a novel and efficient approach to run-time thermal estimation and management for dynamic thermal management in modern microprocessors.
our proposed thermal estimation technique is fast and accurate, and can be used for real-time dynamic thermal management.
the new approach is accurate, fast, and efficient, and is a good candidate for real-time temperature tracking and thermal management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel approach to run-time thermal estimation for efficient dynamic thermal control in lieu of the temperature sensors, which are costly and having longer delays.
our proposed approach can be used for fast thermal estimation in run-time temperature tracking with low overhead, which is very suitable for dynamic thermal management.
the proposed thermal analysis algorithm provides accurate temperature tracking with low overhead and high efficiency for dynamic thermal management.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fast and accurate thermal estimation can be done at architecture level without the need of thermal sensors, which can be used for dynamic thermal management.
the average power profile of the workload is a good indicator of thermal changes and the proposed approach can be used as an alternative to thermal sensors.
the thermal behavior of a chip can be accurately estimated in real-time by a fast algorithm with negligible overhead.
